notes: CBSE does not publish its own Classes 1-5 mathematics syllabus; CBSE schools follow the NCERT textbooks. The 2026-27 prescription was confirmed via official government split-up syllabi (Delhi Directorate of Education; KVS where available) and the NCERT reprint 2026-27 label.

NCERT's 'Learning Outcomes at the Elementary Stage' (tilops101.pdf) could not be opened (robots-blocked); outcomes are written in my own words from the chapter content and the official DoE/KVS split-up outcomes.
Outcomes are not copied from the textbook; questionTypes and difficulty are my judgement.
Textbook is a single annual volume; CBSE has no term split for these books, so term is null. School split-ups (DoE Delhi) divide chapters across mid-term and annual exams, which varies by school.

All 14 chapter titles verified on NCERT's contents page (demm1ps.pdf). Chapter 3 is 'Pattern Around Us' in the contents (CIET audio and the chapter page show 'Patterns Around Us'). Chapter 10 contents prints 'Elephants,Tigers, and Leopards' (missing space corrected).

Section headings were read through the fetch tool's text extraction/summary of each chapter PDF, not by viewing the page; capitalisation is as reported (some headings are printed in capitals). Recurring activity labels ('Let Us Do', 'Let Us Think', 'Let Us Solve', 'Discuss', 'Note for Teachers', 'Project Work', 'Do You Know?') are deliberately omitted.
Chapter 1 sections are incomplete: the extraction only covered pages 2, 5 and 11-15. The circles outcome (centre/radius/diameter) comes from the DoE split-up, not from a heading I saw.
Chapter 2: 'Boxy Buldings' is recorded as the extraction reported it ('sic'); it may be a printing or extraction error for 'Boxy Buildings'.
Chapter 9 (Equal Groups) PDF was robots-blocked: sections [] and outcomes based on DoE split-up (repeated addition, sharing, tables to 10x10).

Chapter 11: extraction reported a 'Complete the designs below' grouping containing 'Symmetry in shapes' and 'Games with a Mirror'; I listed only the latter two plus the other topical headings. 'Floor patterns and the catty wall' and the nature-walk project were reported as headings but omitted as uncertain.
Chapter 12: the chapter has untitled opening sections (calendar/leap year, a.m./p.m. and 24-hour time, clock reading); only the two printed headings are listed.
Chapter 14 PDF also contains the book's Learning Material Sheets (cut-outs, nets, fraction kit); those are not sections.
Chapter 14 bar-graph outcome comes from the DoE split-up; the chapter headings show tables and pictographs only.

outcomes.statement: Describe and classify 3D shapes by their faces, edges and corners and by flat or curved surfaces.
Identify right angles in objects and figures and check them with a folded-paper right-angle tool.
Classify angles as acute, right or obtuse and draw each kind on a dot grid.
Investigate which straw shapes are rigid and count right angles in triangles and quadrilaterals, recognising a square as a special rectangle.
Identify the centre, radius and diameter of a circle.
Match top, front and side views to objects and block buildings, and draw simple views.
Describe positions in a seating layout using rows, columns and ordinal words.

proposed.name: Locate positions and describe routes using grids, maps and directions
proposed.why: MATH.geometry.positions covers relative position words only; grid locations, step-counted paths, map reading and compass directions have no entry.

outcomes.statement: Locate objects on a grid from clues and describe paths with left/right/up/down moves, finding a shorter path.

proposed.name: Locate positions and describe routes using grids, maps and directions
proposed.why: MATH.geometry.positions covers relative position words only; grid locations, step-counted paths, map reading and compass directions have no entry.

outcomes.statement: Read a simple top-view map, identify landmarks and give route directions with turns.

proposed.name: Locate positions and describe routes using grids, maps and directions
proposed.why: MATH.geometry.positions covers relative position words only; grid locations, step-counted paths, map reading and compass directions have no entry.

outcomes.statement: Count arranged collections efficiently by spotting equal groups.
Classify numbers as even or odd by pairing and by the last digit.

proposed.name: Classify numbers as even or odd
proposed.why: Parity (pairing, even/odd sums) is assessed from Grade 4 onward and has no existing entry.

outcomes.statement: Find and describe patterns on a 1-100 number grid.
Show the same amount of money with different combinations of notes and coins.

proposed.name: Make and total amounts with notes and coins
proposed.why: MATH.measurement.money-coins is recognition only and money-change is finding change; composing a given amount in different ways and totalling a purchase is not covered.

outcomes.statement: Read and write four-digit numbers in numerals, words and expanded form using a Th-H-T-O table.
Group and regroup ones, tens and hundreds, and find how much more is needed to make 1000.
Locate and compare four-digit numbers on number lines with different scales.

proposed.name: Locate and compare numbers on a number line
proposed.why: No existing competency covers placing numbers on a number line with different scales or using it to count on and back.

outcomes.statement: Compare and order four-digit numbers using < and > by comparing place values from the left.
Count how many whole numbers lie between two given four-digit numbers.

proposed.name: Locate and compare numbers on a number line
proposed.why: No existing competency covers placing numbers on a number line with different scales or using it to count on and back.

sections.title: Many Ways to Make Halves and Quarters
Let Us Find Fractions in Our Surroundings

outcomes.statement: Divide a shape into halves or quarters in several ways and check that the parts are equal.
Name unit fractions that come from sharing a whole equally and explain that more sharers give smaller shares.
Build fractions such as 3/8 from unit fractions and add unit fractions with the same denominator.
Find a fraction of a collection, such as one-quarter of 12 objects.

proposed.name: Find a fraction of a collection
proposed.why: Existing fraction entries model fractions of a continuous whole; finding a fraction of a set of discrete objects is a separate skill.

outcomes.statement: Recognise equal fractions made by repeated folding, such as 1/3 and 2/6.
Estimate lengths in metres, half metres and quarter metres and check by measuring.
Measure small objects in centimetres with a ruler.
Convert between metres and centimetres and compare lengths written as m and cm.
Find the perimeter of a closed figure by measuring its boundary and draw shapes with a given perimeter on a dot grid.
Add two- and three-digit numbers with regrouping and check by estimating.

proposed.name: Add and subtract multi-digit numbers with regrouping
proposed.why: Existing regrouping entries are for two-digit numbers (Grade 2); there is no entry for 3- to 5-digit column or strategy-based addition/subtraction.

outcomes.statement: Subtract two- and three-digit numbers with regrouping and check by estimating.

proposed.name: Add and subtract multi-digit numbers with regrouping
proposed.why: Existing regrouping entries are for two-digit numbers (Grade 2); there is no entry for 3- to 5-digit column or strategy-based addition/subtraction.

outcomes.statement: Solve shopping problems involving costs, amounts paid, balance and combinations of items within Rs 1000.
Find missing digits in addition and subtraction and solve number-placement puzzles.

proposed.name: Reason systematically to solve puzzles and strategy games
proposed.why: Puzzles and two-player strategy games (e.g. NIM, magic triangles, river crossing) recur across books; no existing reasoning entry targets systematic search or winning-position analysis.

outcomes.statement: Estimate and measure weights in kilograms and grams.
Relate 1 kg to parts such as 500 g, 250 g and 100 g and find how many parts make a kilogram.
Measure and compare capacities in litres and millilitres against 1 litre.
Solve problems with weight and capacity, such as water lost from a dripping tap over a day or week.

proposed.name: Calculate with measured quantities in mixed units
proposed.why: Conversion entries exist, but adding, subtracting, multiplying and dividing lengths, weights and capacities given in mixed units (e.g. 2 kg 300 g) has no entry.

outcomes.statement: Represent multiplication as repeated addition and as arrays of equal rows.
Recall multiplication facts up to 10 x 10.
Divide by equal sharing and grouping and relate division to multiplication.
Solve word problems on equal groups by choosing multiplication or division.
Add four-digit numbers with regrouping in census-style word problems.

proposed.name: Add and subtract multi-digit numbers with regrouping
proposed.why: Existing regrouping entries are for two-digit numbers (Grade 2); there is no entry for 3- to 5-digit column or strategy-based addition/subtraction.

outcomes.statement: Subtract four-digit numbers with regrouping to find increases and decreases.

proposed.name: Add and subtract multi-digit numbers with regrouping
proposed.why: Existing regrouping entries are for two-digit numbers (Grade 2); there is no entry for 3- to 5-digit column or strategy-based addition/subtraction.

outcomes.statement: Round to the nearest ten or hundred to estimate an answer before calculating.

proposed.name: Round numbers to the nearest ten, hundred or thousand
proposed.why: MATH.reasoning.estimate-check covers checking answers by estimation but not the rounding procedure itself.

outcomes.statement: Explore patterns in an addition chart and in reverse-and-add sums, including odd/even rows.

proposed.name: Classify numbers as even or odd
proposed.why: Parity (pairing, even/odd sums) is assessed from Grade 4 onward and has no existing entry.

outcomes.statement: Find winning positions in a two-player adding game (NIM).

proposed.name: Reason systematically to solve puzzles and strategy games
proposed.why: Puzzles and two-player strategy games (e.g. NIM, magic triangles, river crossing) recur across books; no existing reasoning entry targets systematic search or winning-position analysis.

outcomes.statement: Find and count lines of symmetry in shapes and designs.
Predict fold-and-cut designs and complete figures so they are symmetrical about a line.
Describe mirror images of letters, digits and words.
Identify the repeating unit in a tiling and extend it without gaps or overlaps using slides, flips and turns.

sections.title: How many hours in a day?

outcomes.statement: Use a calendar to find days in a month, identify leap years, write dates as DD/MM/YYYY and find ages and durations in days.

proposed.name: Read and use a calendar
proposed.why: No existing entry covers days/weeks/months, finding dates, leap years or counting days on a calendar.

outcomes.statement: Convert times between the 12-hour (a.m./p.m.) and 24-hour formats.

proposed.name: Convert between 12-hour and 24-hour time
proposed.why: No existing entry covers a.m./p.m. and 24-hour time.

outcomes.statement: Calculate elapsed time in hours and minutes.
Read an analogue clock to the minute and relate hours, half hours and quarter hours to minutes.

proposed.name: Convert between hours, minutes and seconds
proposed.why: MATH.measurement.unit-conversions is for metric units; time units are non-decimal and have no entry.

sections.title: Making tables by splitting into equal groups
A Day at the Transport Museum

outcomes.statement: Build new multiplication tables (such as x14, x15) by splitting, doubling and halving known facts.
Multiply by 10, 100 and their multiples using place value.

proposed.name: Multiply and divide by 10, 100 and 1000
proposed.why: No existing entry covers the place-value effect of multiplying or dividing by 10, 100 and 1000 and by their multiples.

outcomes.statement: Multiply two-digit numbers using partial products.
Divide by 10, 100 and by small numbers, finding quotient and remainder.

proposed.name: Multiply and divide by 10, 100 and 1000
proposed.why: No existing entry covers the place-value effect of multiplying or dividing by 10, 100 and 1000 and by their multiples.

outcomes.statement: Solve ticket and money problems that need multiplication.
Collect data with a survey and organise it with tally marks in a frequency table.
Read and complete pictographs and tables and find totals and the largest category.
Interpret a two-way table, such as children who play only one game, both or neither.
Represent data in a simple bar graph and read it.
